Consistency check that confirms the same choice: per-day board unions from -raw are Monday 335, Tuesday 389, Wednesday 257 — every one at or below the 389-board physical grid. The -layout per-day figures are 337/514/202, and Tuesday's 514 EXCEEDS the physical number of boards, so -layout is the lossy extraction here.
Sunday and Thursday return 0 boards, matching the programme text: poster sessions run Monday-Wednesday in Convention Center Level 2 Hall E.

Cross-read of the programme's own wording: 'Poster Sessions ... The papers presented in these sessions meet the same review criteria as lectern-session presentations' — poster items are peer-reviewed contributed papers, not a side track.
cadence_evidence: Annual, each January in Washington DC. The 105th Annual Meeting was held January 2026 and the 2027 exhibitor site advertises the next edition; TRB's own page lists 'January 11-15, 2026' as a single yearly edition. https://events.jspargo.com/TRB27/Public/Content.aspx?ID=123168&sortMenu=103004

alt_figures.basis: phase-1 note, not re-verified this session

character_evidence: Open call for papers with a fixed 1 August submission deadline and full peer review; TRB's own programme states poster papers 'meet the same review criteria as lectern-session presentations'. Author and paper-review resources are public at https://trb.secure-platform.com/a/page/TRBPaperReview
programme_evidence: Three days of poster sessions filling a 389-board hall plus several hundred lectern sessions, all drawn from a reviewed open call; the exhibit hall and Solution Showcase Theater are separately branded vendor content and are excluded
ratio_rationale: Judged 45% for THIS meeting, and the judgement is anchored on TRB's own counted artefact rather than on a comparable from another field. The 2017 programme yields 981 counted poster presentations against a meeting of roughly this size, and lectern presentations sit on top of that at four per lectern session across several hundred sessions — so presenters are a large minority, not a small one. Pushing it below half: the 11,000 headcount is padded by an exhibit floor, a career fair and 400+ standing-committee business meetings, and 30.9% of attendees are public-sector agency staff who come to committee meetings rather than to present, with student attendance at 18.5% cutting the other way since students do present. Not pushed higher, because unlike a Japanese society taikai or a chemistry divisional congress there is a large non-presenting practitioner and policy constituency here. Note this ratio is context only: the row is decided on the counted 981, not on the conversion.
method: Language searched: English (US meeting). 2 searches used, both on the abstract ladder; neither produced the figure. FIGURE PRODUCED BY RUNG 6 (poster-board arithmetic), zero further searches. Route: TRB's open file server onlinepubs.trb.org serves annual-meeting documents but 403s on directory listing, so the filenames were enumerated at zero cost from the Wayback CDX API: https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=onlinepubs.trb.org/onlinepubs/am*&output=text&collapse=urlkey&limit=400&filter=statuscode:200 — that listed TRB_2017_Final_Program.pdf. TRAP HIT AND AVOIDED: the live URL https://onlinepubs.trb.org/onlinepubs/am/2017/TRB_2017_Final_Program.pdf returns HTTP 200 with content-type text/html (150,212 bytes) — it silently serves an error page, not the PDF. Checking status AND content-type caught it; the archived copy at https://web.archive.org/web/20171007015516id_/... returns HTTP 200, application/pdf, 13,574,523 bytes and was downloaded into a private scratch directory. Extracted BOTH ways (pdftotext -layout and pdftotext -raw). The programme prints an explicit board range for every poster session ('CC Hall E, Posters H331-H333, J361-J364'), so the count is the union of expanded board IDs per day, summed over days (boards are reused day to day, so a document-wide union would undercount and a per-session sum would double-count cross-referenced Part 1/Part 2 sessions). Parser: normalise unicode dashes to '-', rejoin ranges broken across lines, split the text on the 'Sessions, Events, and Meetings: <Day>' headers, then regex Posters?\s+((?:[A-Z]\d{2,4}\s*-\s*[A-Z]?\d{2,4}|[A-Z]\d{2,4})(?:\s*,\s*...)*) and expand each range. -raw gives Monday 335 + Tuesday 389 + Wednesday 257 = 981; -layout gives 337 + 514 + 202 = 1,053. THE TWO DISAGREE, so per the method the tie was broken on an independent marker rather than by averaging: the physical board grid. -raw's distinct board IDs form a regular 16-letter grid (A-R skipping I and O) of 25 boards per letter, 389 in total, and no single day exceeds 389; -layout's union is 520 solely because it mis-parses one range as N=150, and its Tuesday figure of 514 exceeds the physical number of boards, which is impossible. -raw is therefore the sound extraction and 981 is the figure. WHAT 981 IS NOT: it is POSTERS ONLY and it is DATED 2017. Lectern presentations are entirely uncounted (the printed programme lists lectern SESSIONS but not their individual papers; TRB's session-planning document states a lectern session 'typically includes no more than four presentations'). A session-count multiplication was attempted and REJECTED as unsound: 3-digit session numbers cannot be separated from room and page numbers in the extracted text (801 candidate matches against ~650 real sessions), so no lectern figure is recorded rather than a bad one. EXCLUDED from the count: exhibit-hall content, the Solution Showcase Theater (30-minute exhibitor product talks), the Career Fair, and 400+ standing-committee business meetings. NEXT ACTION IF A LARGER FIGURE IS WANTED (rung 5, orchestrator): trid.trb.org is server-rendered for page furniture but injects its result list and its 'Showing 1 - N of M records' counter by JavaScript, so curl cannot read a count; open https://trid.trb.org/Results?txtKeywords=%22Transportation+Research+Board+103rd+Annual+Meeting%22 in a browser and read the record total. MyTRB's online programme at https://annualmeeting.mytrb.org/ is a CREDENTIAL wall, not a bot wall — a browser gains nothing there, so do not queue it. Two search snippets asserted 'over 4,000 presentations across more than 650 sessions' (2025) and 'more than 5,000 presentations in nearly 750 sessions' (2026); BOTH WERE REFUSED, because every page offered as their source was opened and none carried the sentence: www.trb.org/Main/Newsletter-241029.aspx, www.nationalacademies.org/events/886 (opened via WebFetch, which confirmed no such figure), trb-annual-meeting.nationalacademies.org, and six Wayback captures of trb.org/AnnualMeeting/AnnualMeeting.aspx from 2023-2024. Absence of that figure from a loadable page is not evidence it is false, only that it is unsourced here.
